citation: Somers, M.-A., Corrin, W., Sepanik, S., Salinger, T., Levin, J., & Zmach, C. (2010). The Enhanced Reading Opportunities Study Final Report: The Impact of Supplemental Literacy Courses for Struggling Ninth-Grade Readers (NCEE 2010-4021). IES/MDRC. ERIC ED511811.
design: RCT (students randomized within 34 high schools; schools randomized to program)
population_location: Grade 9 students reading 2-5 years below grade level; 34 high schools, 10 US districts; 2 cohorts (n=2,916 and 2,679)
program_model: Year-long supplemental literacy course replacing an elective (Reading Apprenticeship Academic Literacy or Xtreme Reading)
partner_runnable: no: school course taught by teachers (school model, not a partner link)
outcome_measure: Reading comprehension (GRADE); state ELA and math tests where given in grade 9; core GPA; credits; grade 10 follow-up
direction: positive in program year; null the following year
effect_as_reported: Fetched executive summary: comprehension ES 0.09; core GPA ES 0.07; core credits ES 0.06; 'students also scored higher on their English language arts and mathematics tests ... effect size of these impacts are 0.11 and 0.07'; in the following school year impacts on GPA, credits and state test scores 'are not statistically significant'.
already_screened: no (S-0256 cites it only as background in an Evidence for ESSA reference list)
notes: Strongest lane 1 result found. State ELA effect only in the subset of states testing in grade 9. Fade-out is the key caveat. Earlier reports: Kemple et al. 2008 ED499778; Corrin et al. 2008 ED503380.

citation: Boulay, B., Goodson, B., Frye, M., Blocklin, M., & Price, C. (2015). Summary of Research Generated by Striving Readers on the Effectiveness of Interventions for Struggling Adolescent Readers (NCEE 2016-4001). IES. ERIC ED560732.
design: Systematic review of 17 grantee RCTs under WWC standards (15 met standards)
population_location: Struggling readers grades 6-10, 16 US districts and states
program_model: Ten supplemental reading interventions (READ 180, Xtreme Reading, Learning Strategies Curriculum, Voyager Passport, REWARDS, Fusion, Read to Achieve, Kentucky Cognitive Literacy Model, Chicago SR, SLIC)
indicators: S12 (high school sites); S6 (middle school sites)
outcome_measure: Standardized reading tests (SDRT, GRADE, MAP, Gates-MacGinitie) and some state tests (OAKS, iLEAP, Virginia SOL, EXPLORE)
direction: mixed: 4 of 10 positive, 6 of 10 no discernible effects
effect_as_reported: Fetched: 'Four of the ten interventions had at least one study showing a positive effect on reading achievement. The remaining six interventions had no discernible effects.'
notes: Useful as the null-weighted summary: most effects are on non-state standardized tests; state test effects are small or null. Site rows K2-03 to K2-07 come from its Appendix C.

citation: Faddis, B. J., et al. (2011). Portland Public Schools' Striving Readers Program: Year 5 Evaluation Report. RMC Research. ERIC ED600852.
design: RCT (meets WWC standards without reservations per Boulay et al. 2015)
population_location: Grades 7-10, 5 middle and 4 high schools, Portland OR; 2+ years below grade level
program_model: Xtreme Reading supplemental course
outcome_measure: GRADE; Oregon state ELA test (OAKS)
effect_as_reported: Per fetched Boulay et al. (2015): GRADE ES = 0.21 and state OAKS ELA ES = 0.09, statistically significant.
notes: Grades 7-10 mixed; check whether high school grades are reported separately. Pair with K2-04 (same model null in grade 9).

citation: Sprague, K., et al. (2012). Springfield-Chicopee School Districts Striving Readers (SR) Program. Final Report Years 1-5: Evaluation of Implementation and Impact. The Education Alliance at Brown University. ERIC ED600926.
design: RCT (two interventions vs business as usual; meets WWC standards without reservations per Boulay)
population_location: Grade 9, five cohorts, 5 high schools, Springfield and Chicopee MA; below 50th NCE on grade 8 screen
program_model: READ 180 and Xtreme Reading supplemental courses
outcome_measure: Stanford Diagnostic Reading Test (district-administered)
direction: mixed: READ 180 positive; Xtreme Reading null
effect_as_reported: Per fetched Boulay et al. (2015): READ 180 'statistically significant positive effect ... (ES = 0.18)'; Xtreme Reading 'non-statistically significant effects'.
notes: Not a state test; check whether MCAS grade 10 ELA was analyzed in the final report.

citation: Cantrell, S. C., Almasi, J. F., Rintamaa, M., & Carter, J. C. (2016). Supplemental Reading Strategy Instruction for Adolescents: A Randomized Trial and Follow-up Study. Journal of Educational Research. ERIC EJ1094051. (Grantee report: Cantrell et al. 2011, Striving Readers Final Evaluation Report: Danville, Kentucky, ED601005.)
design: Multi-cohort RCT over 4 years
population_location: 593 treated and 535 control grade 9 students (plus grade 6), 7 rural Kentucky districts
program_model: Learning Strategies Curriculum (Strategic Instruction Model) year-long supplemental course
outcome_measure: GRADE reading test
direction: positive for grade 9; null for grade 6
effect_as_reported: Fetched abstract: 'Results indicated significant impacts of the intervention on reading achievement for ninth-grade students but not for sixth-grade students.' Boulay: ES = 0.10 (GRADE).
notes: Strategic Instruction Model lead confirmed. Non-state test.

citation: Dimitrov, D., et al. (2012). Year One Evaluation Report/Impact Study: Illinois Striving Readers. ERIC ED600855.
design: RCT (meets WWC standards without reservations per Boulay)
population_location: 514 grade 9 students, 6 high schools in 4 Illinois districts; bottom two quartiles on state reading test
program_model: Voyager Passport Reading Journeys supplemental course
outcome_measure: Gates-MacGinitie; state-administered EXPLORE Grade 9 Reading
effect_as_reported: Per fetched Boulay: 'non-statistically significant effect ... as measured by ... Gates-MacGinitie ... and the state-administered EXPLORE Grade 9: Reading Test'; Appendix table shows EXPLORE ES -0.12.
notes: Null on a high school standardized test.

citation: Loadman, W. E., et al. (2011). Striving Readers Year 5 Project Evaluation Report: Ohio. ERIC ED601053.
design: RCT (meets WWC standards with reservations per Boulay)
population_location: Incarcerated youth ages 15-25 in 7 Ohio Department of Youth Services high schools
program_model: READ 180
outcome_measure: Scholastic Reading Inventory; California Achievement Test
effect_as_reported: Per fetched Boulay: SRI ES = 0.22 and CAT ES = 0.19, statistically significant.
notes: Special population; transfer to community partners doubtful.

citation: Lang, L., Torgesen, J., Vogel, W., Chanter, C., Lefsky, E., & Petscher, Y. (2009). Exploring the Relative Effectiveness of Reading Interventions for High School Students. Journal of Research on Educational Effectiveness, 2(2), 149-175. ERIC EJ866974.
design: RCT (students randomized to 3 interventions or business as usual)
population_location: 1,265 grade 9 students, 89 classes, 7 high schools in one large Florida district
program_model: Intensive reading intervention classes (three commercial programs)
outcome_measure: Florida state reading test (FCAT, criterion-referenced state assessment)
direction: mixed: positive for 2 of 3 programs in moderate-risk group; no differences for high-risk group
effect_as_reported: Fetched abstract: for the moderate risk group 'reliable differences were observed in the state outcome gain scores between two of the intensive interventions and the business as usual control condition (Glass's adjusted delta = 0.27, 0.30)'.
notes: A rare RCT with a grade 9 state reading test as the outcome.

citation: Vaughn, S., Roberts, G., Wexler, J., Vaughn, M. G., Fall, A.-M., & Schnakenberg, J. B. (2015). High School Students with Reading Comprehension Difficulties: Results of a Randomized Control Trial of a Two-Year Reading Intervention. Journal of Learning Disabilities, 48(5), 546-558. ERIC EJ1070914. (Companion: Vaughn et al. 2015, students with disabilities, EJ1074980, g = 0.44.)
design: RCT (four arms: reading, reading plus dropout prevention, dropout prevention only, business as usual)
population_location: Grade 9-10 students who failed the state accountability reading test, Texas
program_model: Two-year daily small-group reading intervention in place of an elective
outcome_measure: Standardized reading comprehension; social studies grades
effect_as_reported: Fetched abstract: 'significant gains on reading comprehension (effect size = 0.43), and improved reading was associated with better grades in social studies.'
notes: Check whether the state test was an outcome; abstract names only reading comprehension. Dropout-prevention arm used a modified Check and Connect (ED564085).

citation: Vaughn, S., Martinez, L. R., Williams, K. J., Miciak, J., Fall, A.-M., & Roberts, G. (2019). Efficacy of a High School Extensive Reading Intervention for English Learners with Reading Difficulties. Journal of Educational Psychology. ERIC EJ1334035 (ED586763).
design: RCT
population_location: Current and former English learners who failed the state test, 3 urban high schools (n=175 treatment)
program_model: Reading Intervention for Adolescents, 2 years, 50 min daily in place of an elective
outcome_measure: Standardized word reading, vocabulary, comprehension
effect_as_reported: Fetched abstract: 'not on standardized measures of word reading, vocabulary, or reading comprehension (g range: -0.09 to 0.06)'.
notes: Null that limits the K2-09 claim for English learners.

citation: Momeni, F., Bhatt, M., & Guryan, J. (2024). Supporting Adolescent Reading Skills through Small-Group Instruction: A Randomized Controlled Trial of a High School Literacy Intervention in Chicago. SREE abstract. ERIC ED663343.
design: RCT (over 2,700 students in 13 CPS high schools, SY2020-21 to SY2023-24)
population_location: Chicago Public Schools high school students with the highest literacy need
program_model: Structured Literacy: small-group daily class using Wilson Reading System, for course credit
partner_runnable: no as tested (school-day class); small-group design resembles tutoring
outcome_measure: Reading scores (test not named in abstract)
effect_as_reported: Fetched abstract: 'Preliminary findings from analysis of the first 3 cohorts suggest the program increased reading scores by 0.20 standard deviations.'
notes: University of Chicago Education Lab. Look for the full report and test name before use.

citation: Davis, M. H., Schoeneberger, J., Rhoads, C., Mac Iver, D. J., Zhang, X., Mac Iver, M., & Spinney, S. (2025). Accelerating Literacy for Adolescents (ALFA): Evaluating ALFA Lab Using a Regression Discontinuity Study. Journal of Research on Educational Effectiveness. ERIC EJ1501932 (ED653931).
design: Regression discontinuity
population_location: 1,378 grade 9 students in high schools in 4 states, over 3 years
program_model: Semester-long extra literacy lab class during an elective period
outcome_measure: Reading achievement; reading motivation and frequency
effect_as_reported: Fetched abstract: 'positive but nonsignificant effects on reading achievement, motivation, and frequency.'
notes: COVID-era attrition and absences cited as reasons.

citation: Fancsali, C., Abe, Y., Pyatigorsky, M., Ortiz, L., et al. (2015). The Impact of the Reading Apprenticeship Improving Secondary Education (RAISE) Project on Academic Literacy in High School. Empirical Education. ERIC ED571000; SREE paper ED566986.
design: Cluster RCT (teachers in 42 high schools, CA and PA)
population_location: High school ELA (grade 9), biology and US history classes, California and Pennsylvania
program_model: Teacher professional development in disciplinary literacy (Reading Apprenticeship)
outcome_measure: ETS scenario-based literacy assessment (Keystone Literature used only for a correlation check)
direction: mixed: positive in biology classes; not significant overall or in ELA
effect_as_reported: Fetched SREE paper: biology ES 0.32 significant; ELA classes ES 0.22 not significant; full sample ES 0.11 not significant. Fetched full report: Keystone Literature scores were used only to correlate with the ETS test (r = 0.66 PA) and 'we were not able to collect individual-level state test scores from many study schools'.
notes: New since S-0687: Keystone Literature was not an impact outcome. Answers the S-0687 note.

citation: Baye, A., Inns, A., Lake, C., & Slavin, R. E. (2019). A Synthesis of Quantitative Research on Reading Programs for Secondary Students. Reading Research Quarterly, 54(2), 133-166. ERIC EJ1210152; EEF version ED612242.
design: Meta-analysis of 69 studies (62 RCTs, 7 strong QEDs)
population_location: Secondary students grades 6-12, US and UK
program_model: 51 programs; categories: tutoring, cooperative learning, whole-school, writing-focused, content-focused, strategies, technology
partner_runnable: partly (tutoring categories); most are school models
outcome_measure: Widely accepted standardized reading measures
direction: positive for tutoring, cooperative learning, whole-school, writing-focused categories; extra reading periods and technology no better
effect_as_reported: Fetched EEF text: paid-adult tutoring weighted ES +0.24 (all 7 tutoring studies in England); volunteer TextNow ES -0.06; writing-focused +0.13; 27 extra-reading-period studies +0.09 vs 42 without +0.10; Reading Apprenticeship family +0.07.
notes: Key caveat: no US secondary tutoring study qualified. The secondary-reading evidence base for partner-run tutoring is thin.

citation: Scammacca, N. K., Roberts, G., Vaughn, S., & Stuebing, K. K. (2015). A Meta-Analysis of Interventions for Struggling Readers in Grades 4-12: 1980-2011. Journal of Learning Disabilities, 48(4), 369-390. ERIC EJ1064370. (Earlier: Scammacca et al. 2007, ED521837.)
design: Meta-analysis (82 effect sizes)
population_location: Struggling readers grades 4-12
program_model: Reading interventions (mixed)
outcome_measure: All measures; standardized measures reported separately
direction: positive but small on standardized measures
effect_as_reported: Fetched abstract: 'mean effect of 0.49 ... The mean effect for standardized measures was 0.21, also much smaller than the 0.42 mean effect reported in 2007.'
already_screened: no (Chang et al. 2025, S-0715, is a different review)
notes: Grades 4-12, not split for high school in the abstract; includes weaker designs.

citation: Herrera, S., Truckenmiller, A. J., & Foorman, B. R. (2016). Summary of 20 Years of Research on the Effectiveness of Adolescent Literacy Programs and Practices (REL 2016-178). REL Southeast. ERIC ED568684.
design: Systematic review using WWC standards (33 qualifying studies)
population_location: General education students grades 6-12
program_model: Adolescent literacy programs and practices
outcome_measure: Comprehension, vocabulary, general literacy, some state tests
direction: positive for 12 programs, none in high school
effect_as_reported: Fetched abstract: '(3) None of the 12 identified programs and practices was conducted in a high school setting'.
proposed_tier: tested (review): evidence gap for high school
notes: Supports a cautious S12 claim.

citation: Daniel, J., Capin, P., & Steinle, P. (2021). A Synthesis of the Sustainability of Remedial Reading Intervention Effects for Struggling Adolescent Readers. Journal of Learning Disabilities. ERIC EJ1294000.
design: Synthesis (10 studies with follow-up)
population_location: Struggling readers grades 6-12
program_model: Remedial reading interventions
outcome_measure: All reading outcomes at posttest and follow-up
effect_as_reported: Fetched abstract: 'g = 0.78 at immediate posttest and g = 0.27 at follow-up'.
notes: Mostly researcher measures; matches the ERO fade-out.

citation: Olson, C. B., Matuchniak, T., Chung, H. Q., Stumpf, R., & Farkas, G. (2017). Reducing Achievement Gaps in Academic Writing for Latinos and English Learners in Grades 7-12. Journal of Educational Psychology, 109(1), 1-21. ERIC EJ1125530. (Earlier trial: Olson et al. 2012, AERJ, EJ960494; standardized writing test d = 0.10.)
design: Cluster RCT (95 teachers, 16 secondary schools)
population_location: Latino and English learner students grades 7-12, large urban low-SES California district
program_model: Pathway Project teacher professional development in text-based analytical writing
outcome_measure: Writing assessment; California High School Exit Exam (grade 10 ELA and math exit exam) pass
effect_as_reported: Fetched abstract: writing effects 'Year 1, d = 0.48; Year 2, d = 0.60' and 'Pathway students had higher odds than control students of passing the California High School Exit Exam in both years.'
proposed_tier: tested (one RCT plus an earlier RCT)
notes: The exit-exam outcome is a state high school ELA test; check whether it is the ELA part or combined.

citation: Fong, A. B., Finkelstein, N. D., Jaeger, L. M., Diaz, R., & Broek, M. E. (2015). Evaluation of the Expository Reading and Writing Course: Findings from the Investing in Innovation Development Grant. WestEd.
url: lead: not fetched directly; cited in fetched Baye et al. EEF review (ED612242)
design: QED (per Baye: qualifying high-quality study)
population_location: Grade 12, California
program_model: Expository Reading and Writing Course (a grade 12 English course)
outcome_measure: California State University Early Assessment/English Placement Test
effect_as_reported: Per fetched Baye et al.: 'Fong ... found significant positive effects of ERWC (ES= +0.13, p<.05).'
notes: Lead: fetch the WestEd report.

citation: Lovett, M. W., Lacerenza, L., De Palma, M., & Frijters, J. C. (2012). Evaluating the Efficacy of Remediation for Struggling Readers in High School. Journal of Learning Disabilities, 45(2), 151-169. ERIC EJ954838.

population_location: 268 intervention, 83 wait-list students with reading disability, high schools (Toronto, Canada)
program_model: PHAST PACES remedial reading (word identification, text structure, comprehension strategies)
outcome_measure: Standardized word attack, word reading, passage comprehension
effect_as_reported: Fetched abstract: 'An average effect size of 0.68 was revealed across these outcome measures.'
proposed_tier: below bar probably (wait-list QED, baseline equivalence unchecked)
notes: Comparable high-income system; not a state test.

citation: Solís, M., Vaughn, S., & Scammacca, N. (2015). The Effects of an Intensive Reading Intervention for Ninth Graders with Very Low Reading Comprehension. Learning Disabilities Research & Practice, 30(3). ERIC EJ1070325.
design: Small RCT (25 treatment, 19 comparison)
population_location: Grade 9 students more than 1.5 SD below norms
program_model: Multicomponent reading intervention by reading teachers
outcome_measure: WJ-III passage comprehension and others
effect_as_reported: Fetched abstract: 'Results indicate no statistically significant differences between treatment and comparison conditions.'

citation: Patten, J. N., & Chapman, S. J. (2021). Passport to the Future: Boosting Academic Outcomes and Citizenship through Urban Debate. ERIC EJ1292006.
design: Comparison of 55 debaters with 220 non-debating graduates (no evident baseline adjustment)
population_location: One racially segregated New Jersey high school, graduates 2011-2018
program_model: University-high school debate mentoring program
outcome_measure: GPA growth; SAT scores
effect_as_reported: Fetched abstract: 'debate graduates experienced a 0.81 GPA growth (2.5-3.31) ... non-debate graduates exhibited a markedly lower 0.10 GPA growth' and 'Debaters scored higher ... overall SAT scores.'
already_screened: no; adds to L-153 as a weak study
notes: Only new debate item. Shackelford (2019, EJ1212750, Baltimore) is pre-adolescent, so it is out of scope. Anderson & Mezuk (2015, EJ1216079) is a mediation follow-up of a study already in L-153.

citation: Gonzalez, N., MacIntyre, S., & Beccar-Varela, P. (2018). Challenges in Adolescent Reading Intervention: Evidence from a Randomized Control Trial (Working Paper 62). Mathematica. ERIC ED587404; issue brief ED582893.
design: RCT
population_location: Struggling readers in 10 secondary schools, Oakland CA
program_model: Leveled Literacy Intervention: small-group pull-out instruction by teachers
outcome_measure: Reading comprehension; state ELA/literacy standards test (Smarter Balanced)
direction: negative on state ELA; null on comprehension
effect_as_reported: Fetched abstract: 'LLI had no impact on students' reading comprehension and a negative impact on their mastery of English language arts/literacy standards. Students who were pulled out of other classes ... were particularly negatively affected'.
notes: Check which grades (secondary, likely 6-9). A warning against pull-out models that take students out of grade-level classes.

citation: Davis, M. H., McPartland, J. M., Pryseski, C., & Kim, E. (2018). The Effects of Coaching on English Teachers' Reading Instruction Practices and Adolescent Students' Reading Comprehension. Literacy Research and Instruction, 57(3). ERIC EJ1177006.

population_location: 130 grade 9 English teachers, 3,160 grade 9 students in struggling high schools
program_model: Literacy coaching of grade 9 English teachers (Talent Development model)
outcome_measure: Student reading achievement (test not named in abstract)
effect_as_reported: Fetched abstract: 'coaching improved teachers' use and quality of recommended literacy practices and increased student reading achievement over the period of a year.'
notes: Effect size and test not in abstract: fetch the full text.
